name: MEP contractors

problems.words: Submittals sit with the consultant for weeks and we can't order material
quick_ideas: List every open submittal with the date sent, so days waiting are visible
Send the consultant one consolidated pending list weekly, so follow-up is documented.

workzap_build.text: A submittal tracker with revision, date sent, consultant status and days waiting, sending reminders and showing the backlog across all projects daily.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many submittals are open across your projects?
problems.free_stops: Status stages and reminder rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each open submittal's sent date with the material need date, so urgent approvals stand out before procurement stalls.
Give one person one pending-submittal list and a fixed weekly chase time, so consultant follow-up happens without gaps.

problems.words: We lose track of which submittal revision is approved
quick_ideas: Keep one folder per service, electrical, plumbing or HVAC, with only the latest approved revision on top
Mark superseded files clearly, so site never works from an old one.

workzap_build.text: Material approval records linked to requisitions, so only approved items and revisions can be ordered.

problems.ask_first: Who updates the submittal register now?
problems.free_stops: How revisions link to ordering is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Check one live project file against the latest approved comments, so you spot where site may still hold an older revision.
Give one person the job of replacing superseded revisions in one agreed place, so site teams pull the current approved issue.

problems.words: Copper cable keeps disappearing and material drifts between projects
quick_ideas: Count high-value cable drums once against issue records, to size the gap
Record every move between warehouse and site stores with sender and receiver.

workzap_build.text: Warehouse and site store stock with transfer logs confirmed at both ends and a leftover-material register for reuse, with gaps flagged as patterns.

problems.ask_first: How do you know what's in the site store versus the warehouse?
problems.free_stops: The stock structure and alert rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which projects request the most extra cable beyond issue records, so loss patterns by site start to show.
Give one storekeeper one transfer notebook for every warehouse and site material move, so project balances stay traceable.

problems.words: Imported panels and chillers arrive late and delay testing
quick_ideas: List imported items with expected arrival next to the programme date they're needed, so clashes show early
Ask suppliers for a weekly shipment status.

workzap_build.text: An import order tracker from PO to warehouse, comparing expected arrival with programme dates for every project.

problems.free_stops: Tracking stages and alerts are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare promised arrival notes against the site need dates for imported equipment, so testing risks are clear before crews wait idle.
Give one buyer one weekly update list for imported items, so everyone works from the same latest shipment picture.

problems.words: Main contractor deducts back-charges we never agreed to
quick_ideas: Keep every back-charge notice with your response in one register
Take the contract question itself to a professional adviser.

workzap_build.text: A billing and retention ledger with a back-charge register and ageing, so the cash impact is clear on every project.

problems.ask_first: What deductions or delays hurt most?
problems.free_stops: Ledger design and reporting are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count recent back-charge notices against matching site diaries, emails and signed work records on one job, so missing support is clear.
Give one office person one notebook for every deduction notice and reply received this week, so cash-impact records stay together.

problems.words: Technicians are on the wrong site and another site is idle
quick_ideas: Put tomorrow's technician-to-site plan on one sheet each evening
Note each technician's main skill, so the right person goes.

workzap_build.text: A technician deployment board with skills, sending each person their site by WhatsApp daily and showing coverage across projects.

problems.ask_first: How many technicians and foremen do you have?
problems.free_stops: Scheduling rules and the skills matrix are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare yesterday's planned site allocation with where crews actually worked, so mismatch patterns show before another site sits idle.
Give one supervisor one evening planning sheet for next-day site allocation, so morning deployment stops changing ad hoc.

problems.words: Testing fails because installation was not done to the drawing
quick_ideas: Ask foremen for photos at key stages before close-up, so issues are seen early
Review failed tests from the last month to see which service keeps failing.

workzap_build.text: You would see installation and testing checklists for each service with photo proof, so you know you are ready for inspection; technical standards stay with your engineers and the authority.

problems.ask_first: What usually causes rework or failed tests?
problems.free_stops: Checklist structure per system is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Look at recent failed test notes beside the latest issued drawing, so you see which work areas repeat drawing misses.
Give one foreman the job of collecting close-up progress photos in one project chat, so checks happen before finishes hide work.

problems.words: As-builts and O&M manuals delay our final payment
quick_ideas: List every handover document needed per project now, so nothing is left for the end
Give one person ownership of the handover pack.

workzap_build.text: A handover document tracker for as-builts, O&M manuals, warranties and certificates, showing what's missing per project.

problems.ask_first: What's normally left at the end of a project?
problems.free_stops: Document lists and status rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one nearly finished project's handover papers against what the client still asks for, so final payment blockers are clear now.
Give one coordinator one running handover file per project, so as-builts and manuals grow during the job not after.

problems.words: Variations from the main contractor are verbal and we lose track
quick_ideas: Ask for every instruction in writing before work starts
List current verbal variations with dates and photos.

workzap_build.text: A variation log with instruction source, photos and approval status, linked to billing.

problems.ask_first: How are extra works recorded on site today?
problems.free_stops: The approval flow and billing link are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count current verbal instructions still lacking supporting notes or photos, so you see how much extra work is exposed.
Give one engineer one variations notebook kept on site, so every verbal instruction is captured the same day.

problems.words: After handover the client calls us for maintenance and nobody tracks the calls
quick_ideas: Give clients one service number, so calls land in one place
Log each call with date and outcome.

workzap_build.text: You would see every service call after handover logged, assigned and tracked, including maintenance contract visits.

problems.ask_first: Do you hold maintenance contracts after handover?
problems.free_stops: Service categories and response rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count maintenance calls from each handed over project this week, so you see which clients create most after handover work.
Give one office person the job of noting each maintenance call in one notebook, so no client issue gets lost.

never_say: Any advice on electrical loads, cable sizing, earthing, fire systems, gas, pressure testing or code compliance; a qualified engineer or the authority decides.
Any help faking test certificates, bypassing authority inspections or swapping unapproved materials.
Any view on back-charge, retention or payment-term disputes; that is for a professional adviser.
Any request to record technicians' names, IDs, visa or salary details.
Anything other than emergency services first for electrocution, fire, gas leak, fall or confined-space incident.

sample_reply.person: What can we do about submittals? The consultant sits on them for weeks and then the delay lands on us.
sample_reply.pi: Yes, there's a good fix here, and you can start this week. 1) Put every open submittal in one list with the date it went out, so days waiting are visible to everyone. 2) Send the consultant that pending list once a week, so your follow-up is on record. Workzap can do this automatically for you: every submittal tracked by revision and status, reminders sent, and a daily view of what's holding each project. Shall I prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
